newsitem.title: USA: Bombing defendant wants family-style pictures.
newsitem.headline: Bombing defendant wants family-style pictures.

text.p: Oklahoma City bombing defendant Terry Nichols wants to be photographed in prison with his wife and three children so potential jurors can see him as a "human being," according to court filings made public Tuesday.
Nichols goes on trial Sept. 29 for the April 19, 1995 bombing of the Alfred P. Murrah federal building in Oklahoma City that killed 168 people.
Last month Nichols' co-defendant Timothy McVeigh was found guilty of the bombing and sentenced to die.
Justice Department prosecutors opposed Nichols' request, saying he should not be allowed "to stage family scenes now simply to impress the jury."
The only pictures the public has seen of Nichols were taken when he was in custody, handcuffed and wearing a flak jacket.
McVeigh's attorneys also had complained about pictures of their client in an organge jail jumpsuit that were disseminated worldwide.

Nichols' lawyers said jurors may need to see that "one of the most important characteristics of Terry Nichols is his love for his family, his wife Marife and his three children, Josh, Nicole and Christian."

Josh is Nichols' teenage son from his first marriage and the other two are from his second marriage to Marife, a Philippine native. Christian was not yet born when Nichols was arrested two days after the 1995 bombing.
Nichols' request was awaiting a decision from federal Judge Richard Matsch, who will preside over the trial.

Nichols' filing said the request was necessary because the warden at the suburban Denver prison where Nichols is being held will not allow his lawyers to bring a camera into the prison without a court order.

Although prosecutors oppose photographs being taken at the prison, they said in their filing that they will not object to jurors seeing family pictures taken before Nichols was arrested that show Nichols is "a loving husband and father ... if they do exist."
